title: This Mom Turned Kids' Chairs Into a Six-Figure Rental Empire
promo_conflict: The guest promotes Bay Area Kids Rentals and its franchise; the host directs listeners to its website and Instagram. The business results are self-reported; no paid sponsor is evident.

stated_problem.quote: And I looked around and there was none of the chairs, tables that I thought would go with the theme.
stated_problem.speaker: Guest

idea.name: Bay Area kids' party rentals
idea.one_liner: Rent child-sized furniture, inflatables and activity setups to families and event planners for parties, with delivery and optional workshops; the business is also beginning to franchise.
idea.customer: Families planning children's parties, event planners, and some corporate event organizers.
idea.offer: A themed selection of children's tables and chairs, ball pits, bounce houses, bumper cars and activity workshops, with optional delivery or customer pickup.
idea.revenue_model: Per-item and package rentals, mileage-based delivery fees, activity workshops, and franchising; franchise fees are not stated.

key_quotes.quote: And I looked around and there was none of the chairs, tables that I thought would go with the theme.
And so I just said to myself, what if I brought this to the Bay Area?

And then I made a list of the different event planners that I could find online. And I just started following them on social media, putting together pictures of our items, sending them a price list, like a menu, telling them what we do all about us, introducing myself.
The best case scenario is I'm covering my costs in about six rentals.
It's called Event Rental System, currently.
I have a team in place who's managing the business essentially and then I'm basically like I'm the owner.
I would have actually started with more items, even faster, even earlier, when I started, I mean, it shows, like I was like, oh, let me just get chairs, I didn't even get tables.

acquisition_channels.details: Posted unboxing and inventory content on Instagram; built a following through event tags, vendor collaborations and party content.
Emailed a professional athlete's wife directly; she connected the business with her event planner.
Followed event planners on social media and sent them item photos and a price list; the exact message method is not stated.
Invested in SEO to send leads to the website, where parents could book.
Worked with event planners and venues on style shoots, with vendor tags and magazine placements.
Received referrals and additional bookings from event attendees and parents.

ideas.delivery: The business stores inventory, takes online bookings or handles inquiries through staff, and delivers rentals using hired drivers and its own vans and trucks. Customers can also pick items up for free. The guest handles ownership and collection design while a manager, drivers, admin/customer-service assistants and a social media manager handle operations.

prices: 50% deposit; full payment one week before event

uk_legal_risk.reason: The guest describes emailing an athlete's wife directly and social outreach to event planners. In the UK, unsolicited marketing email to individuals is restricted, and cold DMs/texts to individuals or sole traders are prohibited. Cold email is limited to corporate subscribers with an opt-out; any cold calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to enquiry and booking data. DMCC Act subscription rules matter if recurring plans are offered; none are described. Employment Agencies Regs 2003 are not indicated by directly hiring staff.
